title: Check yourself: Residency, quotas, logging and the configuration practice

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A project must keep Claude traffic in the EU and use Sonnet 5.5. Which Vertex endpoint setting fits?

options.text: The global value, since it keeps data inside the EU by default for everyone
options.says: Ruled out because "Global endpoints: Dynamic routing for maximum availability" says nothing of keeping data in a geography.

options.text: The European multi-area value, since named places serve older names only
options.says: The page says a specific region serves `claude-sonnet-4-6` only and that the EU needs "the `eu` multi-region endpoint or a `europe-` region", so Sonnet 5.5 takes the multi-region value.

options.text: A specific region such as europe-west4, since it is the strictest choice
options.says: Ruled out because "A specific region serves `claude-sonnet-4-6` only".

options.text: The us value, since Sonnet 5.5 is served there alone in this case
options.says: Ruled out because the rules say "Residency `eu` needs the `eu` multi-region endpoint or a `europe-` region".

questions.stem: A team asks AWS for 8 million input tokens per minute on Bedrock. What do the docs say about getting it?

options.text: It is within the self-service range, which reaches ten million
options.says: Ruled out because the self-service ceiling is "You can request up to 5 million input TPM and 500,000 output TPM", not ten million.

options.text: It is within the default, so nothing more is needed
options.says: Ruled out because "Default quota is 2 million input tokens per minute (TPM)." and 8 million is far above that.

options.text: AWS alone decides, since the quota is a Bedrock matter only
options.says: Ruled out because the approval named is "without additional Anthropic approval", so Anthropic is part of the decision.

options.text: It exceeds the self-service ceiling, so Anthropic must approve it first
options.says: The page says "You can request up to 5 million input TPM and 500,000 output TPM without additional Anthropic approval", and 8 million is above it.

questions.stem: A compliance team wants a record of prompts and completions for Claude on Google Cloud. What do the pages advise?

options.text: Rely on Anthropic to hold the prompts for the customer
options.says: Ruled out because "Turning on this service does not give Google or Anthropic any access to your content."

options.text: Switch on request-response logging for at least thirty days
options.says: The page says "Enable 30-day request-response logging of your prompt and completion activity to track any model misuse by your users."

options.text: Log the prompts alone, since misuse shows up in what users ask
options.says: Ruled out because the page asks for "prompt and completion activity to track any model misuse by your users", not prompts alone.

options.text: Leave the platform's own defaults untouched and set nothing
options.says: Ruled out because "Anthropic recommends that you log your activity on at least a 30-day rolling basis", so the customer keeps the log.
